texts.facts: 1 The present suit has been filed seeking relief of permanent injunction restraining the defendant from infringement of trademark, copyright, passing off, delivery up, damages, rendition of accounts, etc. 2 The facts as averred in the plaint are that the plaintiff is a company organized and incorporated under the laws of France. The plaintiff has authorized her to sign and verify the pleadings, applications, replies, vakalatnama, to depose on oath and to do all necessary acts on behalf of the plaintiff for the proper conduct and prosecution of the instant suit. Ms. Meena Bansal is fully aware of the facts and circumstances of the instant case. 2.1 It is averred that the plaintiff is engaged in the business of manufacture, distribution and sale of a wide range of clothing, readymade garments, footwear, perfume, leather goods, watches, eyewear and other allied/related products (hereinafter referred to as "the said goods" and "the said business"). The plaintiff has been using and manufacturing, marketing, selling, trading under the trademark/label LACOSTE, , , ,, , and its variants and other formative marks/labels since 1933 onwards. It is stated that since the year 1933, the plaintiff has been honestly and bonafidely, continuously, commercially, openly, exclusively and to the exclusion of others, uninterruptedly and in the course of trade and as proprietor thereof being using its said trade mark in relation to its said goods and business and carrying on its said goods and business thereunder and has built up a worldwide and globally valuable trade, goodwill and reputation thereunder and acquired proprietary rights therein. The LACOSTE/CROCODILE items are sold every second worldwide, as per the data prepared by the Lacoste S.A vs Arun Kumar on 28 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/62628162/ 2 plaintiff. 2.3 Thereafter, on 6th March 2020, a Criminal Complaint under Section 63 of the Copyright Act, 1957 was filed against the defendants through the representatives of the plaintiff and subsequently an FIR under no. 0057/2020 dated 06.03.2020 was lodged at the Byatarayanapura Police Station, Bangalore, Karnataka against the defendants. Thereafter, a search and seizure action was conducted by the Police on same day at the premises of the defendants and seized impugned counterfeit tags and labels under the trade mark/label LACOSTE, , , , , , from the premises of defendants (hereinafter referred to as the " impugned Trade Mark/Label"). As a result, ex-parte ad-interim injunction is granted in favour of the plaintiff and against the defendants / respondents / their agents, representatives, distributors, stockists and all other acting for or on their behalf restraining the defendants from manufacturing, marketing, using, selling, trading, etc. or online marketing or using the Trademark/Label 'LACOSTE' as described in paragraph no.3 of the plaint and / or any other word / mark identical / deceptively similar to the said Trademark in relation to handbags, neck tags, printed tags etc., labels, cut-outs, boards, accessories etc. and cognate items to be used in jeans, readymade garments etc. or from doing any work which is likely to infringe the aforesaid Trademark or passing off etc. till 25.08.2020." 4 Pursuant to summons issued, the defendants despite service neither appeared nor filed written statement, were accordingly ex-parte vide order dated 19.03.2021. Thereafter the matter was listed for ex-parte plaintiff's evidence and interim order dated 27.07.2020 was made absolute till the disposal of the suit. 5 In order to prove its case, plaintiff examined PW-1 Ms. Meena Bansal and thereafter closed its evidence. and the same was allowed vide detailed order dated 29.08.2022 and the defendants were granted time to file written statement. 7 The defendants filed their joint written statement inter alia stating that the defendants have never indulged in any nefarious activities and have no criminal antecedents. The defendants have never indulged nor have counterfeited any trademark or copyright or label of any person / company much less as has been alleged by the plaintiff. However, without prejudice and subject to the plaintiff Lacoste S.A vs Arun Kumar on 28 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/62628162/ 8 proving the legality and validity of alleged copyright / trademark / label, it is stated that defendants undertake that they never have nor they shall ever counterfeit and / or infringe trademark or copyright or label of plaintiff. 10 In order to establish its case, the plaintiff examined Ms. Meena Bansal, AR as PW-1, who has tendered her evidence by way of affidavit Ex. PW-1/A and relied upon documents as under:- (i) Representations of the Trademark/Label of plaintiff - Ex. PW-1/1. (ii) Screenshots from the plaintiff's website www.lacoste.com - Ex. PW-1/2. (iii) Photographs of the impugned mark taken during the criminal raid at the premises of defendants - Ex. PW-1/3. (iv) Copy of authentication report - Ex. PW-1/4. (v) Copies of status report, journal copy and registration certificates along with legal proceeding certificates - Ex. PW-1/5. (vi) Advertisements related to plaintiff's trademark - Ex. PW-1/6. (vii) Document showing availability of plaintiff's goods at online marketplaces - Ex. PW-1/7. (viii) Financial document of plaintiff company - Ex. PW-1/8. (ix) News articles - Ex. PW-1/9. (x) Documents showing the availability of plaintiff's goods under plaintiff's brand within the jurisdiction of this court - Ex. PW-1/10. (xi) Defendant's online presence after raid dated 06.03.2020 - Ex. PW-1/12. (xii) Copy of Power of Attorney - Ex. PW-1/13 (OSR). It is further stated that the plaintiff is the proprietor thereof as also of its goodwill and reputation under the statutory and common law. The popularity and demand of the plaintiff's goods under the said trademark grown so rapidly that the unscrupulous traders and manufacturers started counterfeiting the plaintiff's goods under the said trade mark in early thirties itself. The plaintiff fights against counterfeiting as a social responsibility and given the slogan "Fake Crocodile Real Risk" in the early thirties. A fruitful cooperation between the plaintiff and the public authority around the world has resulted in large seizure of counterfeit goods of the plaintiff under the said trademark in Russia, Peru, United States, Greece, Brazil, Chile, Mexico, France, Israel, China, India and other countries. It is further averred that the plaintiff has various LACOSTE BOUTIQUE stores in New Delhi. For instance, one of the plaintiff's exclusive stores is located at N-2, Janpath Road, Connaught Place -110001 New Delhi. The plaintiff invests heavily in R & D and its products are known for their highest standards of quality, safety, innovation and reliability and there is an ever increasing demand therefore. The plaintiff's founder Rene Lacoste was not only the best tennis player of his time but was also an inventor and designer. The plaintiff has been protecting and enforcing its trade mark against pirate use/applications in India. The plaintiff's products as well as information thereon are available to Indians and Indian trade and industry since decades. 2.8 It is further averred that with the advent of e- commerce, the internet and trade there under the plaintiff adopted the said trademark LACOSTE with the crocodile logo as an essential and material part of its email ID and domain Name viz. www.lacoste.in. The plaintiff has been using the said domain names in course of trade and as proprietor thereof globally in relation to its said goods and business and has built up a valuable trade, goodwill and reputation thereunder. The plaintiff has been carrying on and promoting its said goods and business electronically and through E-commerce platforms such as www.amazon.in etc. and over the internet through the said domain names and also through various other intermeddler web- sites which is accessible in India. The term said trademark of the plaintiff includes its domain name. It said said trade mark is a well known Trade Mark within the meaning of Section 2 (1) (zg) of the Act. They are engaged in the large scale business of manufacturing, marketing, soliciting, selling, displaying and trading of tags including hang tags, neck tags, printed tags etc, labels, cut-outs, boards, accessories, machineries and allied and cognate items to be used on jeans, readymade garments, clothings, sports related goods, sports related clothings, and other allied/related products (hereinafter referred to as "the impugned goods" & "impugned business"). in the month of February, 2020, upon receiving credible information, the plaintiff learnt that the defendants are manufacturing, soliciting, selling, marketing and trading the impugned goods under the plaintiff's said trademark/label in the City of Bangalore, Karnataka. A total of 2500 pieces labels of impugned goods were seized from the premises of the defendants. 2.11 It is further averred that the defendants have adopted and started using the impugned trademark/ label in relation to the abovesaid impugned goods and business. The defendants are also using the same trade dress along with the impugned trademark/label in order to give a false description to its impugned goods. It is further averred that the plaintiff's impugned goods i.e. counterfeit tags and labels, manufactured by the defendants are identical to the tags and labels manufactured by the plaintiff and subsequently attached to the original and genuine goods of the plaintiff. The defendants have imitated the entire shape, colour scheme, manner and placement of literary and artistic work on the impugned tags and labels. The impugned trade mark/label adopted and being used by the defendants in relation to their impugned goods and business are identical with and deceptively similar to the plaintiff's said trade mark/label in each and every respect including phonetically, visually, structurally, in its basic idea and in its essential features. The defendants has also copied the artistic features involved in the plaintiff's trade mark/label and is thus, infringing the plaintiff's copyrights involved in its said trade mark. The defendants are also using all kinds of false description on its impugned goods to wrongly link the impugned goods with the plaintiff and to wrongly convey to the public and customers that the impugned goods are coming from the source and origin of the plaintiff. The impugned goods and business thereunder are also of the same/similar/allied/cognate to that of the plaintiff's. 2.12 It is further averred that the defendants are not the proprietor of the impugned trade mark and had adopted and are so using the same in relation to their impugned goods and business and also Lacoste S.A vs Arun Kumar on 28 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/62628162/ 5 reproducing it on their labels and packaging materials etc. and are otherwise dealing with it in the course of trade without the leave and license of the plaintiff. The defendants have no rights to use it in any manner in relation to its impugned goods and business or for any other specification of goods and business whatsoever being in violation of the plaintiff's rights therein. 2.13 It is further averred that the defendants by its impugned adoption and user of the impugned trade mark is violating the plaintiff's aforesaid trade mark and thereby passing off and enabling others to pass off their impugned goods and business as that of the plaintiff as well as diluting the plaintiff's proprietary rights therein. The defendants are further infringing the plaintiff's said trade mark, which is inter alia duly registered under different numbers. 2.14 It is further averred that recently in second week of July, 2020 after the conduct of criminal raid and lodging of FIR [0057/2020 dated 06/03/2020], the plaintiff has been informed through the sources of markets and the trade, that the defendants have again started manufacturing, marketing & soliciting the impugned goods under the impugned trade mark/label in markets of New Delhi viz. Connaught Place, Sarojini Nagar, Naraina, Gole Market, South Extension and adjoining areas. Being aggrieved thereby, the plaintiff caused an inquiry in the market, which revealed that the defendants had not only started manufacturing, marketing, trading, networking and soliciting but also procured orders from some dealers in New Delhi for supplying counterfeit goods under the impugned trade mark/label. The plaintiff also learnt that there has been meticulous planning by the defendants and the other members of the syndicate to sell the counterfeit goods in the markets of New Delhi under the impugned trade mark/label in a clandestine and surreptitious manner. In addition to the above, the plaintiff has further learnt that the defendants are soliciting their impugned goods under the impugned trademark/ label through third party websites such as www.justdial.com and www.indiamart.com. It is stated that despite being aware of the plaintiff's existing rights in its said trademark/ label and the quantum of damages that be awarded against them in the criminal proceedings which stands pending before the Court of Ld. Magistrate, Bangalore, the defendants have again started carrying on their infringing activities and are continuing their infringing activities on a large scale. 2.15 It is further averred that such a use by the defendants of the counterfeit tags and labels under the plaintiff's said trademark/ label, is the very act of counterfeiting a garment and is bound to create a mistaken impression in the minds of the consumer. The consumers may believe the goods to be genuine & original on the basis of such counterfeit tags and labels bearing the plaintiff's trademarks/ labels. Due to the defendants' impugned activities, the plaintiff is suffering huge losses both in business and in reputation and such losses are incapable of being assessed in monetary terms. Unwary purchasers and trade are being deceived as to the origin of goods or business. The defendants' gains are plaintiff's losses. The plaintiff has no access to the defendants' accounts and the defendants are liable to render their accounts to the plaintiff and to make good to the plaintiff the profits and business earned by them. Additionally, the defendants are liable to compensate the plaintiff with damages on account of their activities. The defendants are soliciting the impugned goods manufactured by it through third party websites on the internet such as www.indiamart.com & www.justdial.com which are interactive in nature in nature and can be accessed by general consumers in New Delhi. The plaintiff has a strong and credible apprehension that the defendants will expand their operation under the impugned trading style/ trademark in New Delhi and the threat that the defendants will use the impugned trade marks within the Jurisdiction of this Court is credible and imminent, thus giving rise to a substantial and integral part of the cause of action within the jurisdiction. Further the plaintiff is also carrying on its said goods and business under its said trade mark in New Delhi through its exclusive and special agents/ stores at: LACOSTE EXCLUSIVE STORE, N-2 Janpath Road, Connaught Place New Delhi- 110001 which is well within the jurisdiction of this court. On the strength of aforesaid grounds, the plaintiff has prayed for reliefs in para 43 of the plaint which are as follows :- (a) A decree of permanent injunction restraining the defendants by itself/themselves as also through his/their individual proprietors/partners, agents, representatives, distributors, assigns, heirs, successors, stockists and all others acting for and on their behalf from manufacturing, marketing, using, selling, trading, soliciting, importing, exporting, displaying, advertising, purveying, intending to sell/solicit or on online marketplaces or online websites or through social medias or by any other mode or manner dealing in or using the impugned trade mark/label LACOSTE, , , , , , and or any other word/mark which may be identical with and/or deceptively similar word/mark to the plaintiff's said trade mark LACOSTE, , , , , , in relation to their impugned goods and business of using, trading, selling, manufacturing, marketing etc of hang tags, neck tags, printed tags etc, labels, cut-outs, boards, accessories, machineries and allied and cognate items to be used on jeans, readymade garments, clothings, sports related goods, sports related clothings, and other allied/related products from doing any other acts or deeds which may amount to infringement, passing off, violation of the plaintiff's right, of the plaintiff's registered trademarks as mentioned in paragraph 7 of the plaint. ( b) A decree for permanent injunction restraining the defendants by itself/themselves as the case may be as also through his/their individual proprietors/partners, agents, representatives, distributors, assigns, heirs, successors, stockists and all others acting for and on their behalf from manufacturing, marketing, using, selling, trading, soliciting, importing, exporting, displaying, advertising, purveying, intending to sell/solicit or on online marketplaces or online websites or through social medias or by any other mode or manner dealing in or using the impugned trade mark/label LACOSTE, which may amount to passing off; (c) An order for delivery up of all the impugned finished and unfinished materials bearing the abovesaid impugned and violative trade mark/label or any other word/mark which may be identical with or deceptively similar to the plaintiff's said trade mark/label/trade name including its blocks, labels, display boards, sign boards, trade literatures and goods etc. to the plaintiff for the purposes of destruction and Lacoste S.A vs Arun Kumar on 28 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/62628162/ 7 erasure. (d) A decree for damages for a sum of Rs. 25,00,000/- (Rupees Twenty Five lakhs only) in favour of the plaintiff and against the defendants (e) An order for rendition of accounts of profits earned by the defendants by their impugned illegal trade activities and a decree for the amount so found in favour of the plaintiff on such rendition of accounts. (f) An order for cost of proceedings" The relevant portion of the said order is as under :- "9. It is further submitted that the plaintiff has not approached the court with clean hand and has concealed material facts and circumstances from the court. The suit is not maintainable and is liable to be dismissed with cost. It is submitted that plaintiff vide present suit has sought to invoke the equitable and discretionary jurisdiction of this court in respect of the cardinal principle is that the person who seeks equity must also be equitable, however, in the instant case, the plaintiff is in violation of the cardinal principle in as much as firstly the plaintiff has wrongly invoked territorial jurisdiction of this court, secondly, no cause of action arose within the territorial jurisdiction of this court and the statements made are either based upon surmises and conjectures without any documentary proof or upon future action, which is impermissible in law, thirdly, the valuation of the reliefs has been done arbitrarily and in contravention of law, fourthly, the documents relied upon by the plaintiff does not show any infringement of either of their trademark / label as alleged, fifthly, no document has been filed by the plaintiff to connect the defendants to the alleged infringement of their trademark / label as alleged and lastly the suit is an arm-twisting mechanism derived by the plaintiff to extort money from the defendants and thus the suit is liable to be dismissed in limine with cost. 8 On merits, it is submitted that the defendants have neither indulged into counterfeiting of any goods nor has ever violated the alleged trademark or copyright of the plaintiff. It is then submitted that the plaintiff and its representatives are resourceful and they by stating false and concocted facts have lodged false and frivolous complaint / FIR against the defendants which has led to the defendants suffering serious trauma. It is further submitted that the list on the websites does not in any manner state or portrays the alleged goods of plaintiff being offered or sold by the defendants. Accordingly, it is prayed that the present suit be dismissed with cost. Section 29(1) of the Trade Marks Act provides that a registered trademark is infringed by a person who, not being a registered proprietor or a person using by way of permitted use, uses in the course of trade, a mark which is identical with, or deceptively similar to, the trademark in relation to goods or services in respect of which the trademark is registered and in such manner as to render the use of mark likely to be taken as being used as a trademark. 21 In case of Corn Products Refining Co. vs. Shangrila Food Products Ltd., 1960 (1) SCR 968, the Hon'ble Apex Court observed that question whether two competing trademarks are so similar as to be likely to deceive or to cause confusion is one of the first impression and it is for the court to decide it. The question has to be approached from the point of view of a man of average intelligence and imperfect recollection. 22 In case of Amritdhara Pharmacy vs. Satyadeo Gupta, AIR 1963 SC 449, whether a trademark is likely to deceive or cause confusion by its resemblance to another mark already registered is a matter of first impression and the standard of comparison to be adopted in judging the resemblance is from the point of view of a man of average intelligence and imperfect recollection. What is important to keep in mind that purchaser does not have both the marks lying side by side for comparison and, therefore, chances of deception are strong. 23 Further in case of Laxmikant V. Patel vs. Chetanbhat Shah & Anr., reported in AIR 2002 SCC 275 , on the aspect of riding upon the goodwill of plaintiff and passing off, reliance can be placed upon para 10 of the judgment wherein it was observed that, " 10. a person may sell his goods or deliver his services such as in case of a profession under a trading name or style. With the lapse of time such business or services associated with a person acquire a reputation or goodwill which becomes a property which is protected by courts. A competitor initiating sale of goods or services in the same name or by imitating that name results in injury to the business of one who has the property in that name. The law does not permit any one to carry on his business in such a way as would persuade the customers or clients in believing that the goods or services belonging to someone else are his or are associated therewith. It does not matter whether the latter person does so fraudulently or otherwise. Firstly, honesty and fair play are, and ought to be, the basic policies in the world of business. Secondly, when a person adopts or intends to adopt a name in connection with his business or services which already belongs to someone else it results in confusion and has propensity of diverting the customers and clients of someone else to himself and thereby resulting in injury." Counsel for plaintiff pressed on award of damages and in this regard, he placed reliance on decisions in case of Time Incorporated v. Lokesh Srivastava, 2005 (30) PTC 3 (Del) ; Microsoft Corporation vs. Deepak Raval, MIPR 2007 (1) 72 ; Hero Honda Motors Ltd. v. Shree Assuramji Scooters, 2006 (32) PTC 117 (Del) ; and Adobe Systems Inc. vs. Mr. P. Bhoominathan, 2009 (39) PTC 658 (Del). In case of Time Incorporated (supra), the Hon'ble court observed that punitive damages are founded on the philosophy of corrective justice and as such, in appropriate cases these must be awarded to give a signal to the wrong doers that the law does not take a breach merely as a matter between rival parties but feels concerned about those also who are not party to the list but suffer on account of the breach. 28 Further, in the case of Hero Honda Motors (supra), the Hon'ble court noticing that the defendant had chosen to stay away from the proceedings of the court felt that in such case punitive damages need to be awarded, since otherwise the defendant, who appears in the court and submits its account books would be liable for damages whereas a party which chooses to stay away from the court proceedings would escape the liability on account of the failure of the availability of account books. 29 In case of Microsoft Corporation (supra), the Hon'ble court observed that in our country the courts are becoming sensitive to the growing menace of piracy and have started granting punitive damages even in cases where due to absence of defendant, the exact figures of sale made by them under the infringing copyright and / or trademark, exact damages are not available.

For instance, one of the plaintiff's exclusive stores is located at N-2, Janpath Road, Connaught Place -110001 New Delhi. The plaintiff invests heavily in R & D and its products are known for their highest standards of quality, safety, innovation and reliability and there is an ever increasing demand therefore. 2.8 It is further averred that with the advent of e- commerce, the internet and trade there under the plaintiff adopted the said trademark LACOSTE with the crocodile logo as an essential and material part of its email ID and domain Name viz. www.lacoste.in. The plaintiff has been using the said domain names in course of trade and as proprietor thereof globally in relation to its said goods and business and has built up a valuable trade, goodwill and reputation thereunder. The plaintiff has been carrying on and promoting its said goods and business electronically and through E-commerce platforms such as www.amazon.in etc. and over the internet through the said domain names and also through various other intermeddler web- sites which is accessible in India. The term said trademark of the plaintiff includes its domain name. It said said trade mark is a well known Trade Mark within the meaning of Section 2 (1) (zg) of the Act. Lacoste S.A vs Arun Kumar on 28 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/62628162/ 4 2.9 It is further averred that in view of the plaintiff's proprietary rights both statutory and common law in its said trademark, its goodwill & reputation, and its copyrights, the plaintiff has exclusive right to the use thereof and nobody can be permitted to use the same or any other deceptively similar trade mark/trade name/copyrights thereto in any manner whatsoever in relation to any specification of goods without the leave and license of the plaintiff. 2.10 It is further averred that the defendants are proprietors of the firm under the name and style of "Arun Tags and Labels". They are engaged in the large scale business of manufacturing, marketing, soliciting, selling, displaying and trading of tags including hang tags, neck tags, printed tags etc, labels, cut-outs, boards, accessories, machineries and allied and cognate items to be used on jeans, readymade garments, clothings, sports related goods, sports related clothings, and other allied/related products (hereinafter referred to as "the impugned goods" & "impugned business"). in the month of February, 2020, upon receiving credible information, the plaintiff learnt that the defendants are manufacturing, soliciting, selling, marketing and trading the impugned goods under the plaintiff's said trademark/label in the City of Bangalore, Karnataka. A total of 2500 pieces labels of impugned goods were seized from the premises of the defendants. 2.11 It is further averred that the defendants have adopted and started using the impugned trademark/ label in relation to the abovesaid impugned goods and business. The defendants are also using the same trade dress along with the impugned trademark/label in order to give a false description to its impugned goods. It is further averred that the plaintiff's impugned goods i.e. counterfeit tags and labels, manufactured by the defendants are identical to the tags and labels manufactured by the plaintiff and subsequently attached to the original and genuine goods of the plaintiff. The defendants have imitated the entire shape, colour scheme, manner and placement of literary and artistic work on the impugned tags and labels. The impugned trade mark/label adopted and being used by the defendants in relation to their impugned goods and business are identical with and deceptively similar to the plaintiff's said trade mark/label in each and every respect including phonetically, visually, structurally, in its basic idea and in its essential features. The defendants has also copied the artistic features involved in the plaintiff's trade mark/label and is thus, infringing the plaintiff's copyrights involved in its said trade mark. The defendants are also using all kinds of false description on its impugned goods to wrongly link the impugned goods with the plaintiff and to wrongly convey to the public and customers that the impugned goods are coming from the source and origin of the plaintiff. The impugned goods and business thereunder are also of the same/similar/allied/cognate to that of the plaintiff's. 2.12 It is further averred that the defendants are not the proprietor of the impugned trade mark and had adopted and are so using the same in relation to their impugned goods and business and also Lacoste S.A vs Arun Kumar on 28 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/62628162/ 5 reproducing it on their labels and packaging materials etc. and are otherwise dealing with it in the course of trade without the leave and license of the plaintiff. The defendants have no rights to use it in any manner in relation to its impugned goods and business or for any other specification of goods and business whatsoever being in violation of the plaintiff's rights therein. 2.13 It is further averred that the defendants by its impugned adoption and user of the impugned trade mark is violating the plaintiff's aforesaid trade mark and thereby passing off and enabling others to pass off their impugned goods and business as that of the plaintiff as well as diluting the plaintiff's proprietary rights therein. The defendants are further infringing the plaintiff's said trade mark, which is inter alia duly registered under different numbers. 2.14 It is further averred that recently in second week of July, 2020 after the conduct of criminal raid and lodging of FIR [0057/2020 dated 06/03/2020], the plaintiff has been informed through the sources of markets and the trade, that the defendants have again started manufacturing, marketing & soliciting the impugned goods under the impugned trade mark/label in markets of New Delhi viz. Connaught Place, Sarojini Nagar, Naraina, Gole Market, South Extension and adjoining areas. Being aggrieved thereby, the plaintiff caused an inquiry in the market, which revealed that the defendants had not only started manufacturing, marketing, trading, networking and soliciting but also procured orders from some dealers in New Delhi for supplying counterfeit goods under the impugned trade mark/label. The plaintiff also learnt that there has been meticulous planning by the defendants and the other members of the syndicate to sell the counterfeit goods in the markets of New Delhi under the impugned trade mark/label in a clandestine and surreptitious manner. In addition to the above, the plaintiff has further learnt that the defendants are soliciting their impugned goods under the impugned trademark/ label through third party websites such as www.justdial.com and www.indiamart.com. It is stated that despite being aware of the plaintiff's existing rights in its said trademark/ label and the quantum of damages that be awarded against them in the criminal proceedings which stands pending before the Court of Ld. Magistrate, Bangalore, the defendants have again started carrying on their infringing activities and are continuing their infringing activities on a large scale. 2.15 It is further averred that such a use by the defendants of the counterfeit tags and labels under the plaintiff's said trademark/ label, is the very act of counterfeiting a garment and is bound to create a mistaken impression in the minds of the consumer. The consumers may believe the goods to be genuine & original on the basis of such counterfeit tags and labels bearing the plaintiff's trademarks/ labels. Due to the defendants' impugned activities, the plaintiff is suffering huge losses both in business and in reputation and such losses are incapable of being assessed in monetary terms. Unwary purchasers and trade are being deceived as to the origin of goods or business. The defendants' gains are plaintiff's losses. The plaintiff has no access to the defendants' accounts and the defendants are liable to render their accounts to the plaintiff and to make good to the plaintiff the profits and business earned by them. Additionally, the defendants are liable to compensate the plaintiff with damages on account of their activities. The defendants are soliciting the impugned goods manufactured by it through third party websites on the internet such as www.indiamart.com & www.justdial.com which are interactive in nature in nature and can be accessed by general consumers in New Delhi. The plaintiff has a strong and credible apprehension that the defendants will expand their operation under the impugned trading style/ trademark in New Delhi and the threat that the defendants will use the impugned trade marks within the Jurisdiction of this Court is credible and imminent, thus giving rise to a substantial and integral part of the cause of action within the jurisdiction. Further the plaintiff is also carrying on its said goods and business under its said trade mark in New Delhi through its exclusive and special agents/ stores at: LACOSTE EXCLUSIVE STORE, N-2 Janpath Road, Connaught Place New Delhi- 110001 which is well within the jurisdiction of this court. On the strength of aforesaid grounds, the plaintiff has prayed for reliefs in para 43 of the plaint which are as follows :- (a) A decree of permanent injunction restraining the defendants by itself/themselves as also through his/their individual proprietors/partners, agents, representatives, distributors, assigns, heirs, successors, stockists and all others acting for and on their behalf from manufacturing, marketing, using, selling, trading, soliciting, importing, exporting, displaying, advertising, purveying, intending to sell/solicit or on online marketplaces or online websites or through social medias or by any other mode or manner dealing in or using the impugned trade mark/label LACOSTE, , , , , , and or any other word/mark which may be identical with and/or deceptively similar word/mark to the plaintiff's said trade mark LACOSTE, , , , , , in relation to their impugned goods and business of using, trading, selling, manufacturing, marketing etc of hang tags, neck tags, printed tags etc, labels, cut-outs, boards, accessories, machineries and allied and cognate items to be used on jeans, readymade garments, clothings, sports related goods, sports related clothings, and other allied/related products from doing any other acts or deeds which may amount to infringement, passing off, violation of the plaintiff's right, of the plaintiff's registered trademarks as mentioned in paragraph 7 of the plaint. It is further submitted that the plaintiff has not approached the court with clean hand and has concealed material facts and circumstances from the court. The suit is not maintainable and is liable to be dismissed with cost. It is submitted that plaintiff vide present suit has sought to invoke the equitable and discretionary jurisdiction of this court in respect of the cardinal principle is that the person who seeks equity must also be equitable, however, in the instant case, the plaintiff is in violation of the cardinal principle in as much as firstly the plaintiff has wrongly invoked territorial jurisdiction of this court, secondly, no cause of action arose within the territorial jurisdiction of this court and the statements made are either based upon surmises and conjectures without any documentary proof or upon future action, which is impermissible in law, thirdly, the valuation of the reliefs has been done arbitrarily and in contravention of law, fourthly, the documents relied upon by the plaintiff does not show any infringement of either of their trademark / label as alleged, fifthly, no document has been filed by the plaintiff to connect the defendants to the alleged infringement of their trademark / label as alleged and lastly the suit is an arm-twisting mechanism derived by the plaintiff to extort money from the defendants and thus the suit is liable to be dismissed in limine with cost. 8 On merits, it is submitted that the defendants have neither indulged into counterfeiting of any goods nor has ever violated the alleged trademark or copyright of the plaintiff. It is then submitted that the plaintiff and its representatives are resourceful and they by stating false and concocted facts have lodged false and frivolous complaint / FIR against the defendants which has led to the defendants suffering serious trauma. It is further submitted that the list on the websites does not in any manner state or portrays the alleged goods of plaintiff being offered or sold by the defendants. Accordingly, it is prayed that the present suit be dismissed with cost.
texts.other_lawyer_arguments: ( b) A decree for permanent injunction restraining the defendants by itself/themselves as the case may be as also through his/their individual proprietors/partners, agents, representatives, distributors, assigns, heirs, successors, stockists and all others acting for and on their behalf from manufacturing, marketing, using, selling, trading, soliciting, importing, exporting, displaying, advertising, purveying, intending to sell/solicit or on online marketplaces or online websites or through social medias or by any other mode or manner dealing in or using the impugned trade mark/label LACOSTE, which may amount to passing off; (c) An order for delivery up of all the impugned finished and unfinished materials bearing the abovesaid impugned and violative trade mark/label or any other word/mark which may be identical with or deceptively similar to the plaintiff's said trade mark/label/trade name including its blocks, labels, display boards, sign boards, trade literatures and goods etc. to the plaintiff for the purposes of destruction and Lacoste S.A vs Arun Kumar on 28 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/62628162/ 7 erasure. (d) A decree for damages for a sum of Rs. 25,00,000/- (Rupees Twenty Five lakhs only) in favour of the plaintiff and against the defendants (e) An order for rendition of accounts of profits earned by the defendants by their impugned illegal trade activities and a decree for the amount so found in favour of the plaintiff on such rendition of accounts. (f) An order for cost of proceedings" The relevant portion of the said order is as under :- "9. Section 29(1) of the Trade Marks Act provides that a registered trademark is infringed by a person who, not being a registered proprietor or a person using by way of permitted use, uses in the course of trade, a mark which is identical with, or deceptively similar to, the trademark in relation to goods or services in respect of which the trademark is registered and in such manner as to render the use of mark likely to be taken as being used as a trademark. 21 In case of Corn Products Refining Co. vs. Shangrila Food Products Ltd., 1960 (1) SCR 968, the Hon'ble Apex Court observed that question whether two competing trademarks are so similar as to be likely to deceive or to cause confusion is one of the first impression and it is for the court to decide it. The question has to be approached from the point of view of a man of average intelligence and imperfect recollection. 22 In case of Amritdhara Pharmacy vs. Satyadeo Gupta, AIR 1963 SC 449, whether a trademark is likely to deceive or cause confusion by its resemblance to another mark already registered is a matter of first impression and the standard of comparison to be adopted in judging the resemblance is from the point of view of a man of average intelligence and imperfect recollection. What is important to keep in mind that purchaser does not have both the marks lying side by side for comparison and, therefore, chances of deception are strong. 23 Further in case of Laxmikant V. Patel vs. Chetanbhat Shah & Anr., reported in AIR 2002 SCC 275 , on the aspect of riding upon the goodwill of plaintiff and passing off, reliance can be placed upon para 10 of the judgment wherein it was observed that, " 10. a person may sell his goods or deliver his services such as in case of a profession under a trading name or style. With the lapse of time such business or services associated with a person acquire a reputation or goodwill which becomes a property which is protected by courts. A competitor initiating sale of goods or services in the same name or by imitating that name results in injury to the business of one who has the property in that name. The law does not permit any one to carry on his business in such a way as would persuade the customers or clients in believing that the goods or services belonging to someone else are his or are associated therewith. It does not matter whether the latter person does so fraudulently or otherwise. Firstly, honesty and fair play are, and ought to be, the basic policies in the world of business. Secondly, when a person adopts or intends to adopt a name in connection with his business or services which already belongs to someone else it results in confusion and has propensity of diverting the customers and clients of someone else to himself and thereby resulting in injury." Lacoste S.A vs Arun Kumar on 28 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/62628162/ 13 24 In case of Time Incorporated (supra), the Hon'ble court observed that punitive damages are founded on the philosophy of corrective justice and as such, in appropriate cases these must be awarded to give a signal to the wrong doers that the law does not take a breach merely as a matter between rival parties but feels concerned about those also who are not party to the list but suffer on account of the breach. 28 29 In case of Microsoft Corporation (supra), the Hon'ble court observed that in our country the courts are becoming sensitive to the growing menace of piracy and have started granting punitive damages even in cases where due to absence of defendant, the exact figures of sale made by them under the infringing copyright and / or trademark, exact damages are not available.
